entities.summary: Niccolò Antonio Colantonio was a prominent Italian painter of the Early Renaissance, born in 1420 in Naples, Italy, and died in 1460. He was a native figure in the art scene of Naples, known for his work in the style of the International Gothic movement. Colantonio's artistic style was influenced by the works of Italian masters such as Fra Angelico and Masaccio. He was particularly skilled in the use of tempera and fresco techniques, and his work can be found in various churches and palaces throughout Naples and the surrounding region. Colantonio's legacy can be seen in the works of later Italian artists, including Raphael and Titian, who were influenced by his style and technique. The painter's use of light and shadow, as well as his depiction of the human form, helped to establish the Neapolitan school of painting as a major force in the Renaissance art scene.

entities.summary: Niccolò Antonio Colantonio, born 1420 in Naples, Italy, was a pivotal figure in the Early Renaissance art movement. As a painter, he was deeply influenced by the work of the great masters, including Masaccio and Donatello, and was known for his innovative use of perspective and his ability to capture the subtleties of human emotion on canvas. His most famous works include the frescoes in the Palazzo Reale di Napoli and the chapel in the Monastery of Sant'Onofrio a Ponticelli. Colantonio's legacy extends beyond his own artistic accomplishments, as he played a significant role in shaping the artistic and cultural identity of Naples during this period. His innovative style and techniques influenced generations of artists, including the great Raphael, who credited Colantonio as a major inspiration. As a result, Colantonio's contributions to the development of Renaissance art are still celebrated and studied today.
